# WHEN THEY REPLY

Any reply pauses the sequence. The setter takes it from here, and speed matters more than polish: a draft in minutes, not hours. The reply earned the reward, and the reward is the three questions written only for that lead, so they go first, the same day, with the page under them. Everything below is for the agent and the setter. Draft only. Nothing is sent without Justin's approval, unless he has set an explicit auto send policy for this campaign.

## The rules of every reply

- **Classify first, then answer exactly what they asked.** Use the triage table. Plain, warm, competent. No performing.
- **`{page link}` always means the page with this lead's own ref**, so the booking matches the lead. One link per message, never two.
- **Reward first.** The reward is the three questions written only for this lead, logged at research (item 10) and sent the same day. Any reply that asks for them, from any framework email, follow-up or closer (a yes, a "send it", a "more info", a "tell me more", a call request), gets the three questions first, with the page link (how it works, plus the calendar) under them. The page never goes out alone to a lead whose close promised the questions. Page only is for a reply that asks only how it works (template Tp), or a reply to the thin research Closer 2 that picks the page. F10 and Closer 1 promised no questions, but a yes to either means they want in, and the questions are already written, so they get them too (K, second opener).
- **A question needs an answer.** Where the lead asked something that needs a reply (how much, the catch, camera, time, who are you), one or two plain sentences may sit above the questions. The questions still come before the page link and before any longer explanation.
- **The questions are the lead's own.** Paste the three from the research log. If any of them would fit another business in the category, rewrite it before sending. Never invent a detail to fill a gap.
- **Reply on their channel.** If they ask for a call, call. If they text, text.
- **Times.** Always two specific odd times (10:15, 2:40, never :00 or :30), on two different days, within the next few business days. State the time zone. Only offer times that really have 45 open minutes (15 to chat, then the interview, then the short review call). Odd times look like a real calendar, not a template.
- **Sign off** every reply with `{sender}`, first name only, on its own line. The templates leave it off to stay readable.
- **Who hosts.** If the sending inbox has `hosts_the_interviews` true, write "I host" and "I'd interview you." If false, write "Justin hosts it" and "Justin would interview you," and the questions line becomes "here are the three Justin, who hosts it, would ask you." Never borrow Justin's background in the first person.
- **Money.** No prices, no numbers, no pay line (it stays parked). "No charge" appears only in the how much and what's the catch answers, only when they asked, once per lead. If it was already used in an earlier email or reply to this lead (F3 counts, so most leads have already had it), use "Nothing changes on that front, and I won't pitch you on the call."
- **Same copy rules as the emails.** No dashes, no exclamation marks, no banned words, and never an assumed answer ("if I don't hear back I'll assume..."). Every ask has an easy way out.
- **Video.** The page may still say video coming soon. Cut the video clause from any template until it is live.
- **Never invent.** No past guests, no past episodes, no audience numbers, no promised clients or views.

## Triage table

| They said | Class | Move | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Sure", "send it", "yes", "more info", "send the questions" | Keen | The three questions first, then the page and calendar under them, then 2 times | K |
| "When are you free?", "let's talk" | Keen, wants a call | The three questions first, then 2 times + page, no extra pitch | K |
| "Tell me more", "what is it?" | Curious | The three questions first, then a short plain answer, page, 2 times | T |
| "How does it work?" (and only that), or picks "the page" on the thin research Closer 2 | Curious, process | Short plain answer, page, 2 times. No questions sent; one line says they are ready | Tp |
| "How much?" | Money question (if it could mean time, answer both) | Plain terms, no numbers, then the three questions, then the page | H |
| "What's the catch?", "how do you make money?" | Trust question | Honest and short, terms stated plainly, then the three questions, then the page | C |
| "I'm not good on camera" | Objection | Reassure, then the three questions, then the page | Cam |
| "Is this a podcast?" | Objection | Call it an interview series, then the three questions, then the page | Pod |
| "How long does it take?", "I'm too busy" | Objection | Honest total, the three questions, 2 times | L |
| "I'm not really an expert" | Objection | Name their ninety seconds, then the three questions, then the page | E |
| "What's in it for me?" | Objection | Honest, no outcomes promised, then the three questions, then the page | W |
| "Who else is in it? Can I see one?" | Objection | Never invent, then the three questions, then the page | G |
| "Not right now" with a date | Timing | Accept, set the date, keep it. If they have not had the questions, send them | N1 |
| "Not right now", no date | Timing | Ask to check back in about three months. If they have not had the questions, send them | N2 |
| "Who are you? How did you get my email?" | Source question | One honest answer, the three questions, page, offer to stop | S |
| "Not interested", polite | No | One line, remove, never contact again | X |
| Rude, angry, "be more professional" | No | Remove. No reply. | none |
| "Stop", "remove me", "unsubscribe" | No | Same as polite no, remove at once | X |
| Forwarded to a colleague | Referral | Thank the forwarder, fresh short note to the colleague | F |
| Out of office, auto reply | Auto | Not a reply. No answer sent. Handle per the OOO rules | none |
| Reply months later | Keen | Treat as keen, restart the booking cadence | R |

**Diagnose the mix, not the message.** A few negative replies are noise. Only if replies are mostly negative, look at the list, then the offer, then the copy, in that order. Never pause a campaign with an inbox full of positives because of one angry reply.

## Reward templates

In every template below, `{the three questions}` means the numbered block pasted from the research log, exactly as in K:

> 1. {question 1}
> 2. {question 2}
> 3. {question 3}

**K. Keen (a yes, "send it", "more info", "when are you free", or a reply to F9 or Closer 2). The three questions lead, the page sits under them:**

> Hey {first_name}, here are the three I'd ask you.
>
> 1. {question 1}
> 2. {question 2}
> 3. {question 3}
>
> Yours either way. If you'd like to answer them on the record, here's the page: {page link}. It has a short video and a calendar, and it explains what happens on the call. We chat for about 15 minutes first, and if it feels right we go straight into the interview. Leave about 45 minutes. I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time, or grab whatever works on the calendar.

*Roster false:* "here are the three Justin, who hosts it, would ask you." Everything after stays the same.

*Second opener, for a yes to F10 or Closer 1 (neither promised the questions).* Swap the first line for: "Hey {first_name}, glad you're open to it. I wrote three questions for you from your work, so here they are." Roster false: "we wrote three questions for you from your work."

*"When are you free?"* Same K. The times are the second thing they read, so keep the line about them as it is.

**T. Tell me more (the three questions lead, then the plain answer):**

> Hey {first_name}, sure. Here are the three I'd ask you first.
>
> 1. {question 1}
> 2. {question 2}
> 3. {question 3}
>
> Yours either way. The Real Experts Series is an interview with people at the top of their field about what they've learned. No matter how good AI gets, it can't replace what a veteran knows. We chat for 15 minutes, then do a 20 to 30 minute interview if it's a fit. Our team edits it and cuts short clips. You approve it before we share it with our list and socials. Here's the page: {page link}. If you'd rather talk it through, I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time.

*Roster false:* "Here are the three Justin, who hosts it, would ask you first."

**Tp. How does it work (and only that), or they picked the page on the thin research Closer 2. Page only, no questions sent:**

> Hey {first_name}, sure. We chat for 15 minutes first, then do a 20 to 30 minute interview if it's a fit. Our team edits it and cuts short clips, and you approve it before we share it with our list and socials. Here's the page, with the calendar: {page link}. I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time. The three questions I wrote for you are ready whenever you want them.

*Roster false:* "The three questions Justin, who hosts it, would ask you are ready whenever you want them."

*Tp is the only reply that sends the page without the questions.* If they then say yes, send K. If they answer a question about the interview with anything beyond how it works, send T.

## Trust and objection templates

**H. How much:**

> Hey {first_name}, fair question. There's no charge for the interview, and I won't pitch you on the call. Here are the three I'd ask you, yours either way.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> The first 15 minutes is just the two of us getting to know each other. Here's the page: {page link}. Does {time 1} or {time 2} suit you?

*If the lead already had "no charge" (F3 ran on their route, which is most routes):* swap "There's no charge for the interview, and I won't pitch you on the call." for "Nothing changes on that front, and I won't pitch you on the call." Keep "There's no charge" only for a lead whose route skipped F3.

**C. What's the catch / how do you make money:**

> Hey {first_name}, good thing to ask. There's no charge for the interview and I won't pitch you on the call. Separately, I work more closely with some businesses on referral partnerships, and some people ask about that later. That's never part of the interview. Nothing hidden. Here are the three I'd ask you, yours either way.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> Here's the page if you want to look first or grab a time: {page link}.

*Same swap as H:* if F3 ran on the lead's route, "There's no charge for the interview and I won't pitch you on the call." becomes "Nothing changes on that front, and I won't pitch you on the call."

**Cam. Not good on camera:**

> Hey {first_name}, a lot of the best people in any trade say that. It's a conversation, not a presentation, and we edit out anything that doesn't land. You see it before it goes anywhere. Here are the three I'd ask you, so you can see what kind of conversation it is.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> Here's the calendar if you want to give it a try: {page link}.

**Pod. Is this a podcast:**

> Hey {first_name}, it's an interview series, a conversation on video. We cut short clips for our socials and send the whole thing to our email list. Call it whatever you like. Here are the three I'd ask you.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> The page has the rest: {page link}.

**L. How long / I'm too busy:**

> Hey {first_name}, about 45 minutes in all. We chat for 15 first, and if it feels right we go straight into the 20 to 30 minute interview. In the last few minutes we book a short review call so you see the edit before anything goes out. Here are the three I'd ask you, so you can see what you'd be answering.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> If a full block is hard, pick the quietest slot you have: {page link}. I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time.

**E. I'm not really an expert:**

> Hey {first_name}, the real experts usually say that. {their ninety seconds, one sentence, in their own words, from research}. That's exactly what the interview is for, and I doubt anyone has asked you how you know. I wrote three questions around it.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> Here's the page: {page link}.

**W. What's in it for me:**

> Hey {first_name}, here's the honest answer. You get a well edited interview of what you know, and you see it first. You can share it anywhere you like. We send it to our list and socials too. If somebody watching needs what you do, they'll know where to find you. I won't promise numbers. Here are the three I'd ask you.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> Here's the page: {page link}.

**G. Who else is in it / can I see one:**

> Hey {first_name}, fair to ask. You approve the edit before anything is shared. Here are the three I'd ask you, written only for you.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> The page shows how it runs and what happens before anything goes out: {page link}.

*Setter rule for G:* only name or link a finished episode if it exists, is live, and the guest approved. Until then, this version is the only one. The three questions are the honest sample of what the interview is.

**S. Who are you / how did you get my email:**

> Fair question, {first_name}. I'm {sender}. {host line}. I found you through {honest source: your website, your reviews, whatever the research log lists}, because {the one true reason they fit}. Here are the three I'd ask you, yours either way.
>
> {the three questions}
>
> The page is here: {page link}. If you'd rather not hear from me, say the word and I'll take you off.

*Host line:* hosts_the_interviews true: "I host the Real Experts Series, interviews with people who are the best at what they do." False: "I work on the Real Experts Series, interviews with people who are the best at what they do, and Justin hosts them." The source must be the real one. If the address came from a business database, say "a business database." Never make up a source.

## Not now, no, and the rest

**N1. Not now, with a date:**

> Makes sense, {first_name}. I'll check back {their date}. {If the questions have not gone: "Here are the three I wrote for you in the meantime, yours either way."}
>
> {the three questions, only if not yet sent}
>
> {Page line, only if the questions went just now: "The page is here whenever: {page link}."}

*Keep the date.* Put a reminder on it. On that day send:

> Hey {first_name}, you said to check back around now. Here's the page again: {page link}. I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time, or grab any slot there. If the timing's still off, say so and I'll leave it with you.

**N2. Not now, no date:**

> No problem at all, {first_name}. {If the questions have not gone: "The three I wrote for you are below, yours either way."}
>
> {the three questions, only if not yet sent}
>
> Mind if I check back in about three months? If not, just say so and I'll leave it with you. The page is here whenever: {page link}.

*If they answer yes, set the date. If they say no, treat it as X. If they don't answer, the hold stands:* send one check back at about three months, with a new reason and an easy out, then follow the normal recycle rules.

**X. Not interested (polite), or "stop":**

> Understood, {first_name}. I won't contact you again. Best of luck with everything.

*Then:* add to the global do not contact list, stop every campaign for them, never recycle.

**Rude or angry:** no reply, ever. Remove them the same way as a polite no. If they say spam, report or legal, also flag it to Justin and check where the address came from. One angry reply never pauses a campaign.

**F. Forwarded to a colleague.** Two messages.

To the forwarder, one line:

> Thanks, {forwarder_first_name}. I'll write to {colleague_first_name} and keep it short.

To the colleague. If the forwarder copied them, reply in that thread. If not, send a new thread, subject `passed along`. No link in this first note. They get a fresh lead ref of their own, logged with the forwarder as the source.

> Hey {colleague_first_name},
>
> {forwarder_first_name} forwarded you a note of mine, so I'll keep this short. The Real Experts Series is a 20 to 30 minute interview with people who are the best at what they do, about what they've learned. {one true line about them from research, or leave it out if nothing passes the specificity test}. No pitch, nothing hidden.
>
> Reply with a yes and the three questions I'd ask you are on their way. If it's not for you, no problem.
>
> {sender}

*Roster false:* "Reply with a yes and the three questions Justin, who hosts it, would ask you are on their way."

*Questions for the colleague.* Research the colleague and log their own three questions before the first note goes out, so the keen reply can be answered with K in minutes. If there is not enough to write three that pass the swap test, answer their yes with Tp and say the questions are being written for them. Never reuse the forwarder's questions.

*If you have only a name and no address,* ask the forwarder for it in the thank you line. Never guess an address.

## Out of office

An out of office is not a reply. Send nothing back.

- **If it paused the sequence,** resume it on the return date plus one business day, so the next touch lands on top of their inbox.
- **If it gives a different contact "for urgent matters,"** do not write to that person on the strength of an auto reply.
- **If it says they have left the company,** remove the lead and research the replacement as a new lead.
- **Ticket acknowledgements and "we received your message" autoresponders** are the same: not a reply, no answer.
- **Harvest the return date and the autoresponder text** for the auto responder seed list.

## Late reply

A reply weeks or months after the last touch is a keen reply. Treat it as one: answer what they asked with the matching template, send the reward if it has not gone, and restart the booking cadence at step 1. Do not mention the gap and do not make them explain it.

- Refresh the research first. Same business, same person, same role? If something changed, open with that.
- If they replied within the "check back" window from N1 or N2, that is a keen reply too.
- If we were the slow ones, add one line at the top: "Sorry for the slow reply."

**R. Late reply:**

> Hey {first_name}, good to hear from you. {answer what they asked, in a sentence or two}. {If the questions have not gone: "Here are the three I'd ask you."}
>
> {the three questions, refreshed against the new research if anything changed}
>
> Here's the page: {page link}. I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time, or grab any slot there.

## The booking cadence

After a keen reply, if they haven't booked. It stops the instant they book, reply, or say no. Any new reply goes back through the triage table. Business days only, mornings in their time zone.

| Step | When | What | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Minutes after the reply | The three questions, the answer, the page under them, two odd times | K, T or the matching template |
| 2 | +1 day, not booked | Lost times | Below |
| 3 | +2 days, not booked | A reason written for this company only | Below |
| 4 | +2 days, not booked | Lost times, fresh times | Below |
| 5 | The next business day | Caller or Justin, by phone | Below |

**Step 1** is the K template: the three questions, the page under them, then "I'm free {time 1} or {time 2} your time, or grab whatever works on the calendar." Some people are put off by a bare calendar link, and some never book without one. Give both.

**Step 2, lost times (+1 day).** Release the two old slots first, so this is true. It should read like a busy person, not like "just following up."

> Hey {first_name}, I lost both of those times. Want to grab one on my calendar here: {page link}, or does {time 3} or {time 4} work?

**Step 3, the company reason (+2 days).** One sentence written for this lead only. Use a detail not yet used in any email sent to them, or their ninety seconds, or a story hook from research. It must pass the specificity test. No flattery, no promised clients or views, nothing that could fit another business.

> Hey {first_name}, one more thought on why the 15 minutes might suit you: {company specific reason, one sentence}. {time 5} or {time 6} your time, or the calendar: {page link}.

*Model of the move, not to be copied:* "The other contractors in town call you when they open a basement and find a boiler from 1924, and nobody has ever asked you how you know."

**Step 4, lost times again (+2 days).** Fresh times, with an easy out.

> Hey {first_name}, my calendar got shuffled again. Two fresh times: {time 7} or {time 8} your time. Or pick your own here: {page link}. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it with you.

**Step 5, the phone.** If a business number is on file, Justin or the caller phones. Voicemail:

> Hey {first_name}, it's {caller} with the Real Experts Series. You replied to my note about an interview, and I want to find you a time that works. The page is in your inbox, and my number is {number}.

If there is no number, send this one last note instead:

> Hey {first_name}, I'll stop chasing times so I don't clutter your inbox. The page stays live whenever you want it: {page link}. If it ever makes sense, reply and I'll find a time.

Then stop, tag the lead "replied, not booked," and set a three month recycle with a new angle.

## After they book

- **Confirm** in one line, with the time in their time zone.
- **The day before,** one line and one useful thing: one of their three questions to think about. No new asks.
- **No show:** one plain note with two new times, then the caller.

> Hey {first_name}, you're booked for {time} your time. Talk then.

> Hey {first_name}, see you tomorrow at {time}. Here's one to chew on: {one of their three questions}. No need to prepare anything.

> Hey {first_name}, looks like we missed each other. No worries. {time 1} or {time 2} your time, or pick one here: {page link}.

Log the outcome (booked, showed, interviewed, approved) in the campaign results note, so the next recycle reads it.

## Recycle

- No reply after the full sequence: recycle in about three months with a new angle and a new reward, the review digest (Attack Plan section 4).
- Not now: the date they gave, or about three months.
- Replied, not booked: three months, as in step 5.
- **Never recycle** a no, a stop, or a rude reply.

## Reply QC (the second agent, before anything is sent)

1. Matches the triage class, and answers exactly what they asked.
2. The three questions are in the message (or already went), pasted from this lead's research log, passing the swap test, none invented, and they sit above the page link. The page goes out alone only in Tp.
3. Exactly one `{page link}`, carrying the lead's ref, and at most one link of any kind.
4. Times: two, odd minutes, different days, zone stated, 45 minutes open. No times in X, rude, or out of office handling.
5. No prices, numbers or promised outcomes. "No charge" at most once per lead. The thesis wording appears only in T.
6. No dashes, no exclamation marks, no banned words, no "silence means no."
7. Sender truth: host line matches the roster. Nothing invented about guests, episodes or sources.
8. Reads like a voicemail from a busy person who looked them up.

# INFRASTRUCTURE & LAUNCH CHECKLIST

**Owner:** Deliverability Engineer signs the infrastructure half. The QC Auditor signs the copy half. The Executive Director confirms both. Justin approves the launch.
**Approval rule for this campaign:** this send is under Justin's brand and name. Nothing is bought, no DNS record is changed, no credential is rotated, and no inbox is attached to a campaign without Justin's explicit yes in chat, with the dry run shown first. Read-only checks run freely.
**Status words:** PASS, PULL, FIX, OPEN. Every `[NEEDS: ...]` below is an open item until someone fills it in. Nothing ships with an unfilled placeholder.
**Tooling (house, never rewritten):** `winnr-instantly` skill and its repo CLI (always `--dry-run` first), `dns_check.py` for DNS, Hermes `instantly-deliverability-audit` and `cold-email-weekly-rhythm`, `verify-emails` and `verify-leads` for addresses.

## 1. Decisions, each with its reason

### 1a. Aged domains or lookalike domains: LOOKALIKES, bought early

**Decision:** every sending domain is a lookalike of truerevenuepartnerships.com, bought early. No aged domains in the live set. Aged domains are not used even as insurance, because insurance inboxes can be swapped into live sending the same day and must meet the same brand standard.

**Reason:**
- House rule: anything under Justin's or a client's name uses lookalikes. This campaign is exactly that. Justin's name is in the credibility line (F8), the From name on some inboxes, and the thesis of the series.
- Aged domains break brand continuity. A prospect who looks up the sending domain must land somewhere that clearly reads as True Revenue Partnerships and the Real Experts Series. A random aged domain with an unrelated history cannot do that.
- The follow-ups carry a link to experts.truerevenuepartnerships.com. A sending domain that obviously belongs to the same brand makes that link look like a continuation, not a mismatch.
- The risk of lookalikes is a slow start. That is accepted. Domain age is bought by buying early, so the domain order is the first purchase, ahead of mailboxes.
- Aged domains are reconsidered only if Microsoft inbox placement fails on lookalikes after warmup is complete, and only with Justin's approval.

**Rules for the domain set:**
- `.com` first, `.co` second. No `.net`, `.xyz`, `.io`, `.ai`, and no long multi-word strings. Each domain must read as the brand at a glance, so Justin picks the final names from a shortlist: `[NEEDS: domain list]`.
- Never send from truerevenuepartnerships.com. Never send from the experts.truerevenuepartnerships.com subdomain. The main domain and the booking page host stay clean so a burned lookalike can be dropped without touching them.
- Registrar with flat renewal pricing and a working API. `[NEEDS: registrar choice]`.
- Domains stay on the registrar's own name servers. Not parked behind one shared Cloudflare pair. `[NEEDS: confirm name servers per domain]`.
- Searching each domain must lead to a real-looking site (see 1b).

### 1b. Forwarding or masking proxy: FORWARD AT THE 1,000 TIER, MASKING PROXY AT THE 3,000 TIER

**Decision, by capacity:**
- **1,000 sends a day (18 domains in total, 12 live plus 6 insurance):** forward each lookalike to experts.truerevenuepartnerships.com. This is under the house limit of about 20 domains.
- **3,000 sends a day (51 domains in total, 34 live plus 17 insurance):** masking proxy. Each lookalike serves the Real Experts Series page content on its own address instead of redirecting. Fallback if a proxy per domain is too heavy: one simple microsite per domain.
- **Switch trigger at either tier:** any drop at Level 2 placement, any Level 3 pull that traces to a forwarded domain, or any blacklist flag on a forwarded domain moves that tier to the masking proxy.

**Reason:**
- The house rule allows forwarding under about 20 domains and requires a proxy or microsites above that or when placement drops. Forwarding 51 cold domains to one destination is the exact pattern receivers and blacklists are starting to notice.
- This campaign is brand-sensitive, so the conservative path is cheap insurance: a proxy costs a small hosting service, a flagged brand domain costs far more.
- The destination is the series page, not the root of the main site, because it is the best trust asset: it shows what the interview is, what happens on the call, and the calendar. A prospect who types the sending domain sees the same thing the email described.
- The proxy serves content read-only. The booking button and every email link point to the real page at experts.truerevenuepartnerships.com with the lead's ref, so the ref always carries through to the booking.

**Approval note:** forwarding rules, proxy hosting, and DNS pointing on a domain all count as changes to DNS and need Justin's approval with the dry run shown. `[NEEDS: Justin approval, forwarding or proxy per tier]`.

### 1c. Mailboxes and personas

- **Provider mix:** `[NEEDS: provider mix]`. House starting point is Google Workspace as the base, with SMTP and Microsoft added to spread ban risk. Any Microsoft share sends fewer per mailbox, so the capacity table below must be recomputed if Microsoft is used.
- **Do not buy mailboxes from the sequencer.** No pre-warmed mailboxes under someone else's name or domain.
- **Real person on every inbox:** a real first name, a profile photo where possible, a LinkedIn that exists. `[NEEDS: inbox persona list]`.
- **Roster flags per inbox (open item 5 in the doc):** `hosts_the_interviews` and `justin_background` set true or false for every inbox. An inbox with `hosts_the_interviews` false never writes "I'd interview you". An inbox with `justin_background` false never uses the credibility line in the first person (F8 is third person or skipped). No inbox is attached to the campaign without both flags filled in. `[NEEDS: roster flags per inbox]`.
- **Justin's own name:** which inboxes send as Justin is Justin's call. `[NEEDS: Justin's decision on how many inboxes send as Justin]`.

## 4. Warmup start and go-live criteria

Go-live is gated by criteria, not by a countdown. Every inbox is judged on its own. The warmup start is logged per inbox in the register.

**Warmup settings (set when the mailbox is added):**
- Instantly's premium warmup pool. No free or unlimited warmup tools.
- Slow ramp on. Never 0 to 50 on day one. Warmup volume climbs until it equals that inbox's planned cold volume, then warmup keeps running alongside the cold sends.
- Warmup reply rate set as high as the tool allows (about 25%).
- Insurance inboxes start warming on the same standard and never stop warming.

**An inbox goes live only when every line is true:**
- [ ] Warmup health reads 99 to 100% (an inbox that falls to about 92% comes out of campaigns).
- [ ] Warmup volume has reached the inbox's planned cold volume, with the ramp unbroken.
- [ ] The lookalike warmup floor in `deliverability.md` §7 has been met. The warmup start date is in the register. The date is checked against that rule, not estimated here. `[NEEDS: warmup start date per inbox]`.
- [ ] SPF, DKIM, DMARC and MX pass on the domain, and no blacklist lists the domain or the page host.
- [ ] Seed placement test run from the inbox. Directional only, since seeds never mark spam.
- [ ] Persona complete: name, photo where possible, LinkedIn, roster flags.
- [ ] Domain resolves to its forward or proxy target and the page loads.
- [ ] The campaign's first batch has passed per-lead QC (section 6).
- [ ] Justin has approved attaching the inbox, with the dry run shown.

**Cold volume ramp after go-live:** start each inbox below its planned cap and step up only after the previous step showed Level 1 at 99 to 100%, bounce under 2%, and no placement drop. A step that fails holds or steps back. No step is scheduled by calendar.

## 5. Instantly settings for the 22-step policy

Set these in Instantly for the one campaign (split by time zone or provider only if the sequencer requires it). Items marked `[VERIFY IN UI]` are confirmed by a test send to a seed inbox before launch, never assumed.

**Sequence structure:**
- 22 steps. Odd steps 1 to 19 are framework emails, each a new thread with its own lowercase subject (1 to 4 words, spun). Even steps 2 to 20 are the follow-ups, replies in the same thread, with the subject field empty so they thread. Step 21 is Closer 1, a new thread, subject spun per the Closer 1 block in THE TWO CLOSERS (the single source for that subject). Step 22 is Closer 2, a reply in thread, subject empty. Thin research leads with a shortened route (Research, routing rule) run in separate campaigns with the matching step count, never with blank steps.
- Delay between steps: 3 days after each step, matching the policy (framework, follow-up 3 days later, next framework 3 days after that). `[NEEDS: confirm delays before steps 21 and 22, default 3 days]`.
- Per-lead copy: each lead's 22 touches are written for that lead, so the step bodies and subjects ride in as lead variables. `[NEEDS: confirm the house loading method and variable names with the winnr-instantly CLI, including a variable for the lead ref]`.
- Spintax uses Instantly's format (`{{RANDOM | a | b | c}}`). `[VERIFY IN UI]` that spin sets render inside lead variable values. If they do not, the spins are rendered before upload and the second-agent QC reads the rendered text.
- The preview shows no surviving single-brace `{placeholder}`, no `[bracket]`, and no blank variable on any of the 22 steps. A lead with a blank variable is not loaded.
- The page link on follow-ups and closers resolves to `experts.truerevenuepartnerships.com/?ref=` plus that lead's ref. Framework emails carry no link at all.

**Content and tracking:**
- Plain text only. No HTML, no images, no signature graphic, sign-off is the sender's first name (spun per the doc).
- Open tracking off. Click tracking off. The page link is sent as a plain link, never wrapped in a tracking redirect, so no custom tracking domain is needed.
- Unsubscribe header on for every step. Footer rule: the footer carries the postal address (for US recipients) and nothing else, and the unsubscribe mechanism is the sequencer's unsubscribe header. No opt-out sentence in the footer, because opt-out lines live in Closer 1 and Closer 2 only and a footer line would repeat on every step and echo the closers. The footer is not part of the copy in this doc, so it is excluded from word counts and from the no-link check (`verify_doc.py` reads only the doc). `[NEEDS: postal address, approved by Justin]`.

**Stopping rules:**
- Stop on reply: on. Any reply pauses the lead and hands off to the Reply Setter.
- Stop for the whole company on reply: only for leads on a business domain. Many of these experts use gmail.com or other free mail, and a company-wide stop on a free-mail domain could pause unrelated leads. Either keep this off for free-mail leads or confirm the sequencer separates them. `[VERIFY IN UI]`.
- Stop on auto-reply: off, so an out-of-office does not end a lead's sequence. Auto-replies are harvested into the Level 4 seed list. `[VERIFY IN UI]`.

**Sending rules:**
- Business days only, inside local business hours for the lead's time zone. If the sequencer holds one time zone per campaign, leads are split into campaigns by time zone. `[NEEDS: send window, set by the Analyst]`.
- Per-inbox daily cap from the capacity table. Random gap between sends, not a fixed one. Values logged in the register.
- Only lists that passed `verify-emails` and `verify-leads` are loaded. Catch-all domains get catch-all verification, not a guess. Addresses are the expert's own where possible, never `info@` style role addresses.
- Inboxes are attached only after section 4 is complete for each one, only through the house CLI, only with Justin's yes.

# WEEKLY RHYTHM & HEALTH CHECKS

**Principle for this campaign:** a sudden reply-rate drop is checked in this order. Infrastructure first (Levels 1 to 5 below), then the list, then the copy. Nobody edits a framework or a list until the Deliverability Engineer reports that infrastructure is clean. The 10 frameworks are the test, so a copy change made against sick inboxes ruins the read.

## 1. The five-level inbox health process

Run on every live inbox and on every insurance inbox. Automated through the Hermes `instantly-deliverability-audit` and `cold-email-weekly-rhythm` skills, results logged to the Obsidian vault.

| Level | Check | Rule | Day | Owner | If it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Warmup reputation score | Distrust anything under 99 to 100%. An inbox at about 92% comes out of campaigns. | Daily | Deliverability Engineer | Remove from campaign, keep warming, swap an insurance inbox in (needs Justin's yes, see section 3). |
| 2 | Seed inbox placement test | Directional only, since seeds never mark spam. A drop across several inboxes on one domain matters more than one miss. | Daily | Deliverability Engineer | Check the domain's DNS and blacklists, then treat as a drop alert (section 4). |
| 3 | Real reply rate per inbox and per domain, this week against two weeks ago | At 100 sends or more and under 1% reply rate: pull the inbox. Real human replies only, positive or negative. Auto-replies and bounces do not count. | Friday | Deliverability Engineer | Pull the inbox, cancel it from campaigns, cancel its subscription, swap in insurance. |
| 4 | Auto-responder seed test | Send from each inbox to the seed list of addresses known to auto-reply (out-of-office and "no longer monitored"). Expect about 80% to auto-reply. Under 60%: kill the inbox or the domain. Harvest new auto-responders from this campaign's replies into the list. Use a short neutral note, never campaign copy. | Saturday | Deliverability Engineer | Kill the inbox or domain, swap in insurance. |
| 5 | Always-on likely-positive baseline | Every inbox also runs a campaign that reliably gets positive replies (candidate sourcing, partnership, or podcast-guest outreach). If its reply rate drops on one inbox, that inbox is sick. It is a separate campaign from this one, so a copy problem here is never confused with a sick inbox. | Always on, read Friday | Deliverability Engineer | Treat as a Level 3 failure for that inbox. |

`[NEEDS: seed list source, from Justin's other campaigns, built before the first Saturday check]`
`[NEEDS: baseline campaign and its per-inbox daily volume]`

## 2. The weekly rhythm

| When | Check | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Daily | Warmup scores (Level 1). Seed placement (Level 2). Bounce rate: pause the whole campaign above 3%, target under 2%. | Deliverability Engineer |
| Daily | Every reply answered within minutes during send hours. Booking cadence running: 2 times plus the link, lost-times follow-up at the next day, a company-specific reason, lost-times again, then the caller. Every link carries the lead's ref. | Reply Setter |
| Daily | Recording schedule checked against booked interviews so F7's "a couple a day" stays true. | Reply Setter, with Justin |

## 3. When an inbox fails

1. Cancel it from campaigns. Cancel its subscription. Do not let it keep sending to see if it recovers.
2. Swap in an insurance inbox so volume has no downtime. Swapping in is attaching an inbox to a campaign, so it needs Justin's yes. Ask once for a standing approval with a logged dry run for same-day swaps, so a failure never waits overnight. `[NEEDS: Justin's decision on standing approval for insurance swaps]`.
3. Buy a replacement for the insurance pool. That is a purchase, so it goes to Justin with the dry run.
4. A failed domain is retired. The main domain is never used as a replacement.
5. Log the failure, the level that caught it, and what was done to the Obsidian vault.

## 4. Drop alerts (a sudden fall, for example 1.5% to 0.2%)

- **Spam trap first.** Pull the affected domains now, then trace the list batch that fed them. Experts scraped from local business listings and small-business databases are a spam trap risk, so re-verify that batch, including catch-alls, before it is reused.
- **Fingerprinting second.** Check that the spin sets are actually rendering and add more spintax variety. Because each lead's 22 touches are custom, a drop that follows a templated batch points here.
- **Link third.** Follow-ups and closers are the only touches with a link (the page with the ref). If reply rates fall on even steps only, check the page host's reputation and whether that link is the cause.
- Report levels 1 to 5 for the affected inboxes to the Executive Director before anyone touches the list or the copy.

## 5. The Analyst's weekly read

Logged to the Obsidian vault, in the daily note for the day of the read. `[NEEDS: vault name, so the note opens with an obsidian:// link]`

- **Verdicts at 1,000 sends per variant:** 0 positive replies means kill that variant. 1 positive reply means scale it to 3,000 sends. The variant is the one under test: first the reward wording (Attack Plan section 8), then, one at a time, the lead framework for a segment and the track (A or B).
- **The funnel:** replies, positive replies, page visits by ref, bookings by ref, interviews attended, interviews recorded, edits approved, features published. The campaign's only email goal is a reply. Every later step is read by ref so it traces back to the lead and the framework that opened the conversation.
- **Next test:** chosen from this week's results and the setter's notes from conversations (what experts said when they asked "what's the catch", "is this a podcast", and "not good on camera").
- **Recycle:** non-repliers at sequence end are scheduled for a new angle and the review digest (Attack Plan section 4), per the Attack Plan.
- **Cross-check with infrastructure:** a framework's weak verdict only counts if the Deliverability Engineer confirms the inboxes that sent it passed Levels 1 to 5 that week. A verdict drawn from a sick inbox is voided and the variant is re-run.

# QC CHECKLIST — THE SECOND-AGENT PASS

A second agent, never the writer, runs this on all 22 touches for every lead before inboxes are attached. Any failure sends the lead back to the writer.

1. **Script clean:** `verify_doc.py` reports zero problems on the doc (with the doc's declared `ai` allowance), and `--leads` is clean on the batch.
2. **Attack Plan match:** the review-pattern signal shows up in the lead framework's relevance line, later relevance lines use further distinct Gold or Silver details, and the three questions are the reward in §0, in the framework closes, in F9 and in Closer 2.
3. **Naming:** "Real Experts Series" appears once per framework email, in the offer sentence. Never in a subject. No other company names.
4. **Dashes and exclamation marks:** zero in any copy, subjects and spin options included.
5. **AI footprint and voice:** no parallel three-item lists (terms and feature lines included), no filler openers, sentence length varies, read-aloud passes. Peer to peer, warm, curious. If a line would fit on a marketing page, it fails.
6. **Lengths and grade:** framework emails 85 to 100 words. Follow-ups 30 to 50, ending on one question. Closer 1 under 50, Closer 2 under 100. Reading grade 5 target, 7 ceiling, on every piece.
7. **The detail and the opener:** exactly one research detail per email, in the first two lines, passing the specificity test, logged with a source, never reused across the 22. At most 3 of the 13 relevance lines start with "Saw", and no two frameworks in a row open with the same verb.
8. **One pain:** exactly one pain per framework email.
9. **The close:** at least 8 of 10 frameworks close on the three-questions reward, worded fresh. Every close carries an easy out from the bank, F10 included. No close sentence and no close skeleton (the same opening words and main verb) repeats within a lead, across the framework closes, the follow-up lines that offer the questions and both closers. No out repeats within a lead, in words or in idea (framework-close outs and the F9 follow-up's out; follow-up job lines follow the job table). "No pitch, nothing hidden" does not count as the out.
10. **Follow-ups:** each does the job in the follow-up job table, and none opens with "following up on." The page link appears only in the F1, F4, F7 and F10 follow-ups. Every other follow-up has no link and ends on a question about their craft.
11. **Links and standalone:** none in framework emails. At most one in a closer, and it's the page with the lead's ref. No framework email references another. Each follow-up references only its own framework.
12. **Claims:** no numbers about AI or the internet, no "most" about online content, no promised outcomes, views, audience size or clients, no invented guests or episodes. Nothing about owning the clips or experts in nearby fields seeing it. Regulated fields: no results or advice language. The word AI only in F2, F10, Alt A or the "tell me more" reply, once, as the thesis, or as "an AI summit" inside F8's credibility line.
13. **Money:** no banned words, "fee" and "fees" included. "No charge" exactly once per lead, in F3. "Free" never in a subject. No pay line.
14. **Signature lines and roster:** each line only in its homes and within its limits, never more than three per email. The credibility line is word for word, F8 only, first person only when the sender is Justin, and never mentions referral partnerships. Every first-person host line has a `Roster false:` swap, and inboxes with `hosts_the_interviews` false use it.
15. **Routing:** lead framework matches the selection table. F7 and F9 in the back half, and Alt C, when it runs, in F8's slot. Track B leads with Alt A. Ten passing details run the full 22 touches. Five to nine run that many framework emails (skipped back to front, F1, F9 and the lead kept) plus the closers. Two to four run Alt B, its follow-up and the closers (thin research Closer 2). Fewer than two are skipped. No route reuses or invents a detail.
16. **Spin sets:** every framework has one, with a subject of 3 or more options, the greeting and the sign-off. Closer 1's subject is spun. Every option passes every rule on its own.
17. **Opt-out:** Closer 1 and Closer 2 each carry a plain opt-out line from the closer bank. Nothing says "silence means no."
18. **Touch 1 read twice:** the lead framework's example (F1 by default) is the best email in the doc. If it isn't, fix it first.
